Yoshita et al Table 2 p 585 marks visual hallucinations yes/no for each of 14 clinically diagnosed DLB patients; no frequency measurement and no fig intervention or exposure.

Doubleday et al p 602 reports visual hallucinations in 71% of 41 DLB patients at investigation; p 603 reports no history in 26 Alzheimer's comparators. No hallucination episode frequency or fig exposure; visual distractibility is separate from hallucinations.
Publisher-provided original text of retrospective four-patient progressive aphasia series describes neck dystonia and dystonic hand posture; no fresh sage exposure or comparative effect.
Publisher-provided original text describes limb and axial rigidity in progressive aphasia patients; no ground sage exposure or comparative effect.

Full 2002 KJR paper (Materials and Methods/Results; 15 patients) measures parkinsonian tremor and MRS after unilateral thalamotomy; it does not measure rigidity severity. Ground sage was not studied. Generic introductory listing of rigidity is not an observed outcome.
Yoshita et al Table 2 p 585 records visual hallucination presence or absence in 14 DLB patients; neither hallucination episode frequency nor salmon exposure is measured.

Doubleday et al p 602 reports visual hallucinations in 71% of 41 DLB patients and p 603 no history in 26 Alzheimer's comparators; no frequency measure or salmon exposure. Visual distractibility and intrusions are separate cognitive findings.

Retrospective PD chart and autopsy series records visual hallucinations in 24 of 38 over the disease course; Table 1 reports 8 of 17 versus 16 of 21 by cognitive group, not episode frequency. No grilled salmon exposure; Salmon is a cited author.

Full 1976 JNNP case series (pp.1210-1218) describes an anticonvulsant-treated trigeminal-neuralgia patient with pain exacerbation and difficulty eating (Case 3, p.1214); no pain scale and no food/date exposure. Related pain-history context only, not evidence for dried date or a Parkinson outcome.

Full identity-matched 1999 EHP case report (pp.417-422) is a painter with chronic mixed-solvent exposure. Physical examination (p.418) found normal sensory responses including pain; no pain-severity endpoint and no date/food exposure. Excluded as non-food solvent-encephalopathy context.
Bonifati et al p 532 case RM612 had mild bilateral upper-limb resting tremor at examination; brother RM611 had no tremor. No fig exposure or food comparison.
Yamada et al p 111 case had postural hand tremor with resting tremor explicitly absent on exam; no fig exposure. No effect on resting tremor is demonstrated.

Full 2002 KJR report measures medically refractory parkinsonian tremor by a 0-4 Tremor Rating Scale preoperatively and about 4 months after thalamotomy. Baseline: 3/15 scored 2, 10/15 scored 3, 2/15 scored 4; follow-up: 13/15 scored 0 and 2/15 scored 1, with abolition in 13/15. The scale includes action/postural tremor and is not a rest-specific score; no fig exposure. Related motor outcome context only.
PD drug-addition study mentions resting tremor as background and reports total motor scores, not a separate tremor result; no raw fig exposure.

Yamada et al p 111 case showed mild bradykinesia with reported improvement after trihexyphenidyl; UPDRS motor total 33 to 18 over four weeks, not an item-specific numerical change. No salmon exposure or comparison.
The PD neuropathology cohort describes bradykinesia and other motor signs without a grilled salmon exposure or a food-related severity contrast.

Whelan et al Table 1 pp 1544-1545 lists bradykinesia as primary symptom for two of five Parkinson DBS patients and records Hoehn-Yahr pre/post stage, but no bradykinesia item severity comparison or salmon intake.

Whelan et al p 1545 notes no preoperative indicators of anxiety or depression in five DBS patients; no anxiety scale or severity comparison, and no salmon exposure. Study outcomes are linguistic tasks, not anxiety.

Full 1976 JNNP report describes increased apathy during phenobarbitone/phenytoin toxicity (Case 2, p.1213) and a separate patient described as slow/apathetic during phenytoin intoxication (Case 5, p.1214); these are clinical observations without an apathy rating scale. Epilepsy/toxic-drug context, no date exposure or PD treatment.

Full identity-matched 1999 EHP case report (pp.417-422) describes a painter with solvent-related cognitive deficits, irritability, anxiety and depression; formal mood testing assessed anxiety/depression, not apathy. The Discussion (p.420) names apathy as a general feature of chronic toluene encephalopathy, not a measured outcome in this patient. No date/food exposure.
